observations.title: An untrusted prize can leave the NFT winner without a terminal exit after sponsor allocation
observations.description: The exported specification treats arbitrary prize contracts as untrusted, while IRaffle narrows supported prizes to honest standards-compliant ERC721s. A prize can satisfy the factory's initial interface, callback and owner checks yet reject a later outgoing transfer. Once the VRF callback sets NftWon, enableRefunds rejects that status. Permissionless settlement allocates 95% to the sponsor and 5% to the treasury without attempting delivery, and those allocations can be released independently. The owner's redemption correctly rolls back its burn when transferFrom or the ownership verification fails, but there is no subsequent refund or alternate terminal exit, so the winner can retain only an indefinitely unredeemable ticket while the sale pot has been paid out. Under the exported untrusted-prize model this is a liveness and economic trust-boundary gap. Clarify whether permanently transferable honest prizes are a precondition; otherwise the design needs an explicit terminal-delivery failure policy that preserves the intended allocations and independent claims.
assumptions: Arbitrary untrusted prize contracts may escrow successfully and later make outgoing transferFrom revert or make the post-transfer ownerOf check fail.
The reserve is met, the trusted wrapper resolves before its deadline, and settlement is completed.

The intended untrusted-prize guarantee includes a usable terminal outcome despite a prize transfer becoming unavailable. If honest permanently transferable prizes are the intended support boundary, the finding is instead a specification/documentation mismatch.
This observation does not claim reentrancy, unauthorized USDC withdrawal, or failure of EVM rollback. No executable adversarial artifact was constructed.

observations.title: Sponsor prize release can transfer an NFT into a clone registered after recipient validation
observations.description: Initialization screens sponsorRecipient once using the current factory registry, and code-less destinations are not queried. A currently unregistered future clone address can therefore be accepted as the immutable recipient. If that address later becomes a registered clone, releaseSponsorPrize still transfers the prize with raw transferFrom and only checks that ownerOf equals the configured recipient; it does not repeat the protocol-destination screen used by quote payouts. The transfer can succeed into the other clone without its ERC721 receiver hook, mark prizeClaimed true, and leave an unrelated NFT in a contract with no rescue route. This violates the stated prohibition on moving assets between raffle clones even with an honest prize token. Screen the current recipient at sponsor-prize release as well, and define how recipient configurations that later become invalid should be handled.
assumptions: The immutable sponsor recipient is selected as an address that is not the current clone and is not yet registered, but is later deployed as a clone of this same factory before prize release.
The original raffle reaches CashWon or Refunding and the prize has ordinary ERC721 transferFrom semantics.

The impact is loss of the sponsor-directed prize and violation of clone isolation; the source does not show theft from an unrelated honest user's raffle or impairment of the other clone's accounted USDC.
No address calculation, deployment, transaction, or executable reproduction was performed.
